slides.title: Crema: the foam that fools you
slides.subtitle: What it really is, and when to trust it.

slides.title: Crema is trapped gas
slides.body: Roasting leaves carbon dioxide inside the beans. Pressure pushes it into the water. When the espresso comes out, it turns into tiny bubbles held together by coffee oils.

slides.title: Why fresh coffee foams more
slides.body: That gas slowly escapes after roasting. The older the beans, the less gas is left, so the foam gets thinner.

slides.myth: Lots of crema means a great espresso.
slides.truth: Not on its own. Crema is a hint about freshness, not a verdict on flavor. The cup is the real test.

slides.title: Crema: a clue, not a score
slides.body: It is gas held by oils. Read it as a hint, then taste.
slides.cta: Save this for your next shot
